Hello,

I'm working my way through the ggplot2 book right now. On page 30,
Figure 3.2, there are some examples of using geoms that "don't make
sense" for the data. One of these is a bar graph. Even though I
realize this is just for illustrative purposes, I do not know how to
construct this graphic. My naive guess was:

qplot(displ, hwy, data = mpg, colour = factor(cyl),
geom = "bar")

but this does not work. I get the error:

Error in pmin(y, 0) : object 'y' not found

I did create a graphic that looks similar by including stat = "identity"
in the qplot call, but it's still not quite right, as the y values are
still cumulative.

Any ideas?

Thanks!
Erik Iverson
